strengths: Clearly identifies and formalizes an important, understudied problem (contextual contradictions in text-to-image generation) with well-motivated examples and intuitive motivation

Comprehensive experimental validation across three benchmarks with quantitative (GPT-4o alignment, Table 1), qualitative (Figures 6-15), and user study components (1,464 evaluations); demonstrates consistent 4-6% improvements in alignment
Sound methodology naturally aligned with diffusion process structure (coarse-to-fine decomposition); clear intuition for why stage-aware injection helps resolve conceptual conflicts
Training-free and practical approach requiring no model retraining; seamlessly integrates with existing FLUX and SD3.0 models; demonstrates robustness across different LLMs (Table 5)
Thorough reproducibility with detailed LLM instructions, full benchmark construction details, VLM evaluation protocol, and in-context examples provided; enables future work
Honest failure analysis with categorization of failure modes (Table 7) and discussion of method limitations; ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrate importance of key components
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: LLM-based decomposition and stage-aware prompt injection are straightforward applications of existing techniques; main contribution is problem formulation rather than algorithmic innovation
Modest empirical improvements: Table 1 shows 4-6% gains over baselines, which while consistent, are incremental rather than transformative; lacking statistical significance testing

Evaluation methodological concerns: (1) GPT-4o alignment metric is somewhat subjective (Table 13 scoring rubric has interpretive aspects); (2) User study samples only 24 of 40 ContraBench prompts; (3) Missing comparisons with simpler alternatives (naive multi-stage prompting, non-decomposed LLM re-prompting)

Narrow problem scope with unclear generalization: ContraBench contains only 40 ChatGPT-generated prompts (potential construction bias); method fails on ~33% of cases (Table 7); applicability to open-ended contradictions and diverse contradiction types unclear

Insufficient technical justification: (1) Stage selection (Table 8) lacks ablation studies; (2) Why coarse-to-fine alignment resolves conceptual conflicts not rigorously analyzed; (3) Decomposition arbitrariness evident in Table 10 examples; (4) No analysis of proxy prompt fidelity to intermediate semantics

Limited analysis of method behavior: No computational cost quantification; missing correlation between decomposition complexity and success rate; baseline methods (R2F, Annealing) tuning details absent; evaluation limited to FLUX/SD3.0—robustness to other architectures unknown

Generalization limitations: Problem-specific to certain prompt types; method entirely dependent on base model capabilities; only visual synthesis tested; no evaluation of diversity-quality trade-offs or cross-style evaluation
Presentation issues: Figures 13-15 have dense text with readability problems; limited discussion of theoretical underpinnings; some design choices appear ad-hoc rather than principled
